rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the action is exclusive to the named subject, adding a negative alternative is awkward; remembrance belongs to people of understanding, unlike an action others can also perform.
rows.anchor: إذا كان الفعل بعدها فعلا لا يصح إلا من المذكور ، ولا يكون من غيره كالتذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negation after إنما excludes a competing agent, while negation before it corrects which person acted; the verse gives the former pattern.
rows.anchor: فمثال التأخير ما تراه في قولك : إنما يجيء زيد لا

words: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنما does more than make إن grammatically inoperative: إن عمرا جاءني does not convey that Amr, rather than Zayd, was the one who came.
rows.anchor: لو قلت : ما جاءني زيد ، وإن عمرا جاءني ؛ لم يعقل منه أنك أردت

words: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These restrictive formulations indirectly condemn those who lack understanding or reverence as irrational and effectively unreachable by warning, rather than merely identifying the audience.
rows.anchor: المعنى على أن من لم تكن له هذه الخشية فهو كأنه ليس له أذن تسمع وقلب يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An active participle presents a settled posture, whereas a verb suggests renewed action or effort; thus the dog is described as lying with paws extended, not as repeatedly extending them.
rows.anchor: الفعل يقتضي مزاولة ، وتجدد الصفة في الوقت . ويقتضي الاسم ثبوت الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb suits qualities still changing, such as a growing child or plant; a noun suits an established state such as a person's settled height.
rows.anchor: وإنما تقول : يطول ويقصر ، إذا كان الحديث عن شيء يزيد وينمو كالشجر والنبات والصبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction illustrated by the opening example is usually heavy, but when it avoids affectation it becomes delicate and witty.
rows.anchor: ولا شبهة في ثقل ذلك في الأكثر ، ولكنه إذا سلم من الاستكراه لطف وملح .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mu'tazz, al-Khalidi, Abu Tammam, and al-Mutanabbi supply examples whose beauty comes from carefully composed phrasing.
rows.anchor: خذها ابنة الفكر المهذب في الدجى والليل أسود رقعة الجلباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor of being bound by someone's kindness is commonplace even in ordinary speech; its poetic beauty comes from the path taken in composition.
rows.anchor: الاستعارة في أصلها مبتذلة معروفة ؛ فإنك ترى العامي يقول للرجل يكثر إحسانه إليه وبره له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excellence of nazm arises from grammatical meanings, their relations, and the purpose and placement of the words; no form is inherently excellent in every context.
rows.anchor: بل ليس من فضل ومزية إلا بحسب الموضع ، وبحسب المعنى الذي تريد ، والغرض الذي تؤم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing and arranging grammatical meanings resembles selecting and placing dyes to create a distinctive image; poets differ in this judgment and arrangement.
rows.anchor: كذلك حال الشاعر والشاعر في توخيهما معاني النحو ، ووجوهه التي علمت أنها محصول النظم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some poems accumulate their effect across several lines, while a single masterful verse in other poems can reveal the poet's skill and command at once.
rows.anchor: ومنه ما أنت ترى الحسن يهجم عليك منه دفعة ، ويأتيك منه ما يملأ العين ضربة ، حتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling someone all people or worth a thousand men attributes to him a sum of virtues found among others without denying those virtues to them.
rows.anchor: تدعي له جميع المعاني الشريفة المتفرقة في الناس من غير أن تبطل تلك المعاني ، وتنفيها عن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling someone simply the brave or generous claims unique excellence, making others' courage or generosity seem unworthy of the name; the cited poems illustrate this hyperbole.
rows.anchor: فإنك تدعي له أنه قد انفرد بحقيقة الشجاعة ، وأنه قد أوتي فيها مزية ، وخاصية لم يؤتها أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed reading that present tears secure lasting union and future tearlessness fails: it makes the speaker seek present crying in order to become like an eye incapable of tears.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك لا يستقيم ويستتب لأنه يوقعه في التناقض ويجعله كأنه قال : أحتمل البكاء لهذا الفراق عاجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dry eye is not a recognized sign of joy or contentment, so it cannot carry the proposed meaning of lasting happiness.
rows.anchor: جمود العين دليل سرور ، وأمارة غبطة وكناية عن أن الحال حال فرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With sound composition, meaning reaches the heart as the wording reaches the ear; faulty composition delays understanding, and extreme obscurity becomes verbal complexity that consumes meaning.
rows.anchor: كان وصول المعنى إلى قلبك تلو وصول اللفظ إلى سمعك . وإذا كان على خلاف ما ينبغي وصل اللفظ

rows.speaker: البحتري
rows.claim: Asked whether Muslim or Abu Nuwas was the better poet, al-Buhturi chose Abu Nuwas and said judging poetry belongs to practiced poets, not scholars who study it without making it.
rows.anchor: البحتري قال حين سئل عن مسلم وأبي نواس : أيهما أشعر ؟ فقال : أبو نواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eloquence cannot belong to wording independently of meaning; likewise, brevity cannot be a property of bare wording, since brevity means few words indicate much meaning.
rows.anchor: لا معنى للإيجاز إلا أن يدل بالقليل من اللفظ على الكثير من المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Word meanings cannot simply be increased or reduced; apparent concision comes when one meaning indirectly points to another that would take many words to state directly.
rows.anchor: يتوصل بدلالة المعنى على المعنى إلى فوائد لو أنه أراد الدلالة عليها باللفظ لاحتاج إلى لفظ كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prestige, repetition, and inherited consensus can make even an obvious error seem authoritative, discouraging experts from examining the flawed theory that eloquence resides in wording alone.
rows.anchor: ولا كان يرسخ في النفوس هذا الرسوخ ، وتتشعب عروقه هذا التشعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed wording 'do not say our gods are three' presupposes multiple gods and contradicts the denial; the author allows a formulation denying that they have three gods or two.
rows.anchor: كانوا قد دفعوا هذا النفي ، وخالفوه وأخرجوه إلى المناقضة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wording can mean not to treat God, Christ, and his mother as three objects of worship; ordinary usage calls two joined to one 'three' and one joined to another 'two'.
rows.anchor: ثم إن هاهنا طريقا آخر ، وهو أن تقدر : ولا تقولوا الله والمسيح وأمه ثلاثة .

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Hassan is reported as saying that anyone whose hand benefits the Prophet must be thanked.
rows.anchor: وروي من وجه آخر أن حسان قال : يا رسول الله من نالتك يده وجب علينا شكره .

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the Prophet often asked for her verses; after she recited a poem on repaying kindness, he reported God's teaching that thanking God requires thanking the person through whom the benefit came.
rows.anchor: ومن المعروف في ذلك خبر عائشة رضوان الله عليها أنها قالت : كان رسول الله كثيرا ما يقول : ' أبياتك '

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: When Sawda recited a poem, Aisha and Hafsa thought it targeted their clans; the Prophet clarified that it concerned the Adi and Taym of Banu Tamim, and the poet was Qays ibn Ma'dan al-Kalbi.
rows.anchor: فأخبر النبي فدخل عليهن وقال : ' يا ويلكن ! ليس في عديكن ولا تيمكن قيل هذا .

rows.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
rows.claim: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar reports that the Prophet corrected a man's recitation from 'Abd al-Dar to 'Abd Manaf and affirmed that was how he had heard the poem.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي : ' يا أبا بكر أهكذا قال الشاعر ؟ ' قال : لا يا رسول الله ، ولكنه قال

rows.speaker: النابغة الجعدي
rows.claim: The source cites a report of the Prophet appreciating poetry: al-Nabigha al-Ja'di recited a verse about his ancestors' glory reaching heaven and hoping to rise further; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وأما ارتياحه للشعر ، واستحسانه له فقد جاء فيه الخبر من وجوه . من ذلك حديث النابغة الجعدي ؛ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ideal brother or friend can be evoked through imagined qualities without referring to a known person; the source illustrates this with poetic wishes and al-Ma'mun's offer to trade the caliphate for such a companion.
rows.anchor: على أنك قدرت إنسانا هذه صفته ، وهذا شأنه ، وأحلت السامع على ما يعن في الوهم دون أن يكون قد عرف رجلا بهذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Zayd is the one who departed' resolves uncertainty about who performed a known departure; 'the one departing is Zayd' identifies a person seen at a distance.
rows.anchor: فإذا قلت : زيد المنطلق ، أزلت عنك الشك ، وجعلته يقطع وبأنه كان من زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting an active participle or attribute makes it identify its bearer rather than assert a quality already visible, as when brocade identifies a familiar person.
rows.anchor: فمتى رأيت اسم فاعل أو صفة من الصفات قد بدىء به فجعل مبتدأ ، وجعل الذي هو صاحب الصفة في المعنى خبرا فاعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is mistaken to infer from dictionary glosses that a figurative expression has no merit over a direct equivalent; figurative speech gains an extra semantic step by using one meaning to indicate another.
rows.anchor: وكان من المركوز في الطباع ، والراسخ في غرائز العقول أنه متى أريد الدلالة على معنى فترك أن يصرح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Much ash in the cooking pot' first denotes frequent cooking and then signifies hospitality, so it carries two indications; 'much hospitality' states the meaning directly and carries one.
rows.anchor: كما ترى من أن الذي هو معنى اللفظ في قولهم : هو كثير رماد القدر . غير الذي هو معنى اللفظ في قولهم : هو كثير القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dictionary gloss lacks this advantage because its obscure term and its explanation share one meaning; there is no second meaning for the original expression to indicate.
rows.anchor: لأن الفضل كان في مسألتنا بأن دل لفظ المفسر على معنى ، ثم دل معناه على معنى آخر .
